title: Replace the placeholder subheading in the home page hero, which is still live
description:
The home page hero subheading currently reads, live today:

"Talk about structured channels, cohort communication, and affordable pricing."

That is a brief to a copywriter, not copy. It tells the reader what the page intends to discuss instead of telling them anything. It sits directly under "Built for Bootcamps and Learning Communities", in the first thing every visitor reads, above the Try for free button. Verified on https://zedu.chat/ on 24 October 2026.

This task replaces that one string. It is not the headline work: T-74 covers headline options and blocks to cut, and T-77 covered headline, subheadline and CTA sets. Neither removed this placeholder, and it is still live.

Deliverable:

1. Three replacement subheadings, each 12 to 25 words, written to follow the existing H1 rather than repeat it. Each must tell a programme manager what Zedu does for them and for whom, and each must work when read immediately after the H1 out loud.
2. For each one, a line on which part of the brief's focus it serves, and the live page that backs every product word in it.
3. A recommendation: which of the three to ship, and why, in two sentences.
4. The file and line to change, from the public zeduchat/zedu-fe repository (the code is under src/, not app/), so the fix can be applied without hunting for it.
5. Confirm whether the same placeholder string appears anywhere else, for example on a solutions page or in the French or Pidgin and Yoruba string sets already delivered, and list every place it does.

Rules: only facts on a live zedu.chat page. Do not use a statistic; the site's proof points are not yet reconciled. No per-student fee wording, no Enterprise price, no claim that the AI replaces instructors. Do not change the H1.
rationale: The focus is acquiring bootcamps, and the hero is where that is won or lost. The subheading under the bootcamp headline is currently an instruction to a copywriter rather than copy, so the most-read sentence on the site tells a programme manager nothing. It is one string, it is verified live, and no existing task has removed it.
reviewBlocker: The task has no delivery waiting for review.
